query: Explain Q-learning like I'm a backend dev who never took an AI class. I'd also like a quick refresher on expectation and variance, because the math in the update rule loses me.
Quantize our ResNet-50 to int8 so it fits on a Jetson, then stand it up behind a REST endpoint our app can call.
For a fraud classifier where 1% of transactions are positive, should I report precision, recall, PR-AUC or ROC-AUC? And do the predicted probabilities need calibrating before the risk team uses them?
I want to train a LoRA on Llama 3 8B using our past support replies so it picks up our tone. Once that's done, how do I tell whether it's actually better than the base model?

Our demand forecast model has been in production since March and the planners say its numbers have felt off for a few weeks. Separately, finance wants to know why it predicted such a big spike for store 114 last Tuesday.
internal wiki Q&A bot — need: chunking + embedding setup, vector index, and protection against instructions hidden inside the wiki pages

Before the fraud model ships I want a GitHub Actions job that fails the PR if AUC drops below the current one — but first, how should I be logging each training run so there's something to compare against?
prophet forecast of weekly call-center volume for Q1 + is last year's Black Friday bump statistically significant or just noise?
Impute the missing ages with the median, one-hot encode city, standardize income and tenure, and make sure nothing from the test split leaks into the fit.

Writing my first custom Dataset for a folder of spectrogram .npy files — what's the idiomatic way? After that I want mixed precision and a warmup LR schedule in the loop. Also, honestly, I still don't get what Adam does that plain SGD doesn't.

Help me design the function schema for an agent that opens Jira tickets, limit what it's allowed to touch in our tracker, and then go through a few of its runs to see whether it's picking the wrong tools.

We want 'customers also bought' suggestions on the product page, built from click logs. The web team needs it as an HTTP service they can call. And once it's live, I'd like a weekly check that warns us if user behavior shifts away from what it was trained on.
loan approval model — per-applicant SHAP explanations, a disparate impact check across age bands, and scrubbing SSNs and home addresses out of the training table
What's the right way to compute recall@5, MRR and nDCG on our retriever, and also check whether each answer cites the passage it was actually drawn from?

I need to summarize 80-page vendor contracts. Before I start, can someone explain how self-attention works so I understand why there's a context limit at all? Then I'd also like the model to spit out the key clauses as JSON reliably.

Tune the XGBoost params with Optuna — though before that I should probably settle on the right metric, since only 2% of rows are positive. Oh and I want to add a few ratio features like debt-to-income first.

Marketing asked us to 'find our ideal customers' and I'm not sure if that's a clustering job or something we should predict. If it's clustering, the revenue columns have gaps and are on completely different scales — how do I fix that first? And how do I decide how many groups to go with?

Our HR-policy RAG bot keeps citing the wrong handbook section. First help me work out whether retrieval or generation is at fault, then fix the chunking, and finally rewrite the system prompt so it says 'I don't know' when the passages don't cover the question.
Add gradient clipping, a cosine LR schedule with warmup, AMP, and early stopping with checkpoints to this training loop.
End-to-end plan for a late-payment predictor: pin down the label and what success looks like, train a first model, ship it as a service, and keep an eye on it for drift after launch.

Fine-tune a detector on our shelf photos with flips and crops that keep the boxes aligned; also, quick explainer on receptive fields? After training, export to ONNX and wrap it in a FastAPI service on the store's edge box.

We're building a customer-support assistant. Start with a few-shot prompt for tone, then give it tools to look up orders and issue refunds, test whether it calls the right one with the right arguments, and make sure nobody can hijack it by pasting instructions into a support email.
Log the params, metrics and the model artifact for every run, then pull up a side-by-side of the runs and register whichever one scored best.

Get a feature store going so the training job and the live API see the same feature values, add CI tests that check the data schema on every PR, and log the weekly retraining runs to MLflow. Oh — and before any of that, the raw extract has a ton of missing values that need imputing.

sensor data project, quick qs: LSTM or transformer for 2k-step sequences? how bad does attention cost get as length grows? numpy broadcasting error in my sliding-window code. also want a SARIMA baseline to compare against.
